forecastReasoning.narrative:
Progressive Cold Front governs the 12Z Day 1–12Z Day 2 period. The 12Z Day 1 issuance carries a MRGN maximum, with Slight-or-greater probabilities covering 0% of the domain. The primary corridor peaks near 21Z Day 1, when mean initiation reaches 64% and expected storm coverage reaches 10%.

A progressive front supplies broad linear forcing while the prefrontal warm sector narrows with time. A representative corridor sounding contains about 802 J/kg CAPE, 574 m²/s² SRH, 97 kt deep-layer shear, 929 m LCLs, STP 1.9, and VTP 1.1. Flow increases from roughly 32 kt at 850 mb to 83 kt at 500 mb and 110 kt at 250 mb.

Maximum probabilities are 2% tornado, 5% hail, and 5% wind; damaging wind is the leading hazard signal. The analog ensemble has high agreement (93% confidence; 30 members), with mean moisture return 90%, clearing 72%, forcing 79%, and cap persistence 23%. Most likely failure modes are storms become linear early (100%).
supportingFactors: Coherent synoptic pattern and frontal geometry (99%)
Strong low-level hodograph curvature (574 m²/s² SRH)
limitingFactors: Sparse expected storm coverage (10% corridor mean)
No hazard probability reaches a concentrated severe threshold
Storms become linear early (100% analog-ensemble signal)
